evidence.text: On 2026-09-11, about 10 weeks into the 13-week Q3, CFO Matt Steinfort said in the $725m equipment-financing release that DigitalOcean 'remains highly confident in our guidance for Q3 and the full year 2026 as well as in our outlook for 2027'. That is an in-quarter company reaffirmation of the $304-307m Q3 guide and the 2027 50%+ frame, made after the 2026-08-01 GPU price increase and the MKC1 (Kansas City, B300) launch were already in the quarter. Consensus sits at the top of the guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: DOCN beat its revenue guide top in Q1 2026 (stock +40.4%) and Q2 2026 (+1.35% on the print day, after a 2026-07-07 pre-release that moved it +4.32%). 6 of the last 8 prints closed up.
evidence.why_not_priced: The stock fell from about $135 (late September) to $91 after this statement, on sector credit fears and with no company-specific negative news found. If the market were treating the quarter as at risk, the consensus would have moved below the top of the guide. It has not (revenue estimates are flat over 60 days per Investing.com). So the statement is in the price for the quarter, but the drawdown and the skew are not pricing a quarter miss. Lands inside the guided range, so small.
evidence.independence: Same company voice as the 2026-08-04 8-K guide. Independent: the bar from two estimate sources sits at the top of the guide (Investing.com 2026-11-02; Earnings Whispers 2026-10-26).

evidence.text: The beat pattern is documented: Q2 2026 revenue was $281.2m against a $272-274m guide (+2.6% over the top), and non-GAAP EPS was $0.45 against a $0.20-0.23 guide. Q1 2026 EPS was $0.44 against $0.26 consensus. Q3 contains a full quarter of the on-demand and 12-month reserved GPU price increase effective 2026-08-01 (company blog 2026-07-21, citing 'strong demand for advanced GPU capacity'; Earnings Whispers calls it a ~30% increase) and the MKC1 Kansas City B300 region, live by 2026-08-04. A repeat beat of +1.5-2.5% would give revenue of about $311-314m against a $306.7-307.2m bar. The EPS whisper of $0.41 against $0.32-0.33 consensus means the EPS beat is already expected by the buy side.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: A Q1 2026 beat and raise: +40.4%. A Q2 2026 beat of $7m over the guide top plus a FY raise: +1.35% (pre-released). 2025-11-05: +18.0%. 2025-08-05: +28.9%. Revenue beats have mostly been bought on this name.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus revenue sits at the guide top ($306.7m), not above it, although the company beat the top by $7m last quarter and Q3 carries a price increase the guide may only partly include. If a repeat beat were priced, revenue consensus would sit near $312m. On EPS it is priced: the whisper is $0.41.
evidence.independence: The price-increase fact comes from a different document: https://www.digitalocean.com/blog/price-changes-gpus (2026-07-21). The Q2 guide comes from the Q1 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001582961/000158296126000045/a2026-q1dopressrelease.htm. Peer pricing: Nebius raised on-demand H100 pricing 17-21% from 2026-10-01 (https://www.spheron.network/blog/nebius-gpu-price-hike-2026-h100-to-b300-rates-rise-up-to-21/).

evidence.text: The 2027 bar sits above management's frame. The CEO said 2027 growth would be above 50% (2026-08-04 8-K), while Investing.com's 2026-11-02 preview says 'some analysts model 60% to 70%' depending on capacity timing and on-demand pricing. Earnings Whispers says the Street 'bets beyond guidance'. If the print reiterates '50%+' without lifting it, the stock may read that as below the top-end models. A lift to 60%+ would be a large positive.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2025-05-06 print fell 13.8% (a guide-driven reaction). The Q1 2026 guide raise drew +40.4%. Guidance has driven the large moves on this name.
evidence.why_not_priced: A stock down 50% from its high is not pricing 60-70% growth. But sell-side price targets (mean $173.80) still embed the top-end models, so a reiterated 50%+ could bring target cuts. The sign is genuinely two-sided, which is why this is sized small. The CFO's 2026-09-11 'highly confident in our outlook for 2027' is the counterweight, and the size is net of it.
evidence.independence: Earnings Whispers via Finviz, 2026-10-26 (https://finviz.com/news/408173/digitaloceans-ai-surge-faces-a-stiff-test-as-street-bets-beyond-guidance), points the same way ('Street bets beyond guidance'). The CFO statement (finding 1's source) points against it.

evidence.text: Funding: UBS estimates DOCN needs about $4bn of incremental capital through mid-2029 to reach about 300 MW. The 10-Q shows $2.76bn of uncommenced co-location leases starting July 2026 to June 2028, $312.3m of 2026 converts due 2026-12-01 (conversion price $178.51, out of the money, so a cash repayment), cash of $767.0m and $406.7m of undrawn revolver at June 30. DOCN raised equity twice in 2026 ($888m follow-on in March, a 12.5m-share direct offering at $117.54 in July). What the money buys is answered: RPO of $894m (more than 10x a year earlier), 155 MW committed, and the $725m (+$300m accordion) equipment facility of 2026-09-11 funds 2027-28 capacity. So this is funding of visible demand, not distress. The residual risk is an equity or convert offering announced with or just after the print, at a price $26 below the July offering.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: April 2026: shares slid on the upsized ~$800m offering (QuiverQuant). July 2026 direct offering at $117.54, alongside the note repurchase. The August 2025 convert offering: shares -10% intraday.
evidence.why_not_priced: The 33% drawdown on sector credit fears is plausibly already pricing a funding overhang. A raise in the window would still be a fresh supply event. A print showing funded capacity could relieve the overhang instead. Net close to zero.
evidence.independence: UBS capital estimate via Investing.com, 2026-11-02 (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/digitalocean-earnings-on-deck-as-ai-funding-questions-loom-93CH-4992298). Financing facility: https://pulse2.com/digitalocean-secures-725-million-equipment-financing-facility-led-by-mufg-axos-bmo-and-wells-fargo-to-expand-ai-cloud-capacity/ (2026-09-11).

evidence.text: The October drawdown is identified as sector contagion rather than company news. Neocloud credit stress (CoreWeave CDS at distress levels, CoreWeave -36% in October, Nebius about -27%), Musk's 2026-10-26 'guppy-level death' remark and Microsoft's 2026-10-28 capex below estimates all hit the group. DOCN fell -8.5% on 2026-10-14 on volume 91% below average and -10.1% on 2026-10-16, with no company release. DOCN's AI customer ARR is $234m of $1,125m total ARR (about 21%), so most of the business is the core developer cloud, which these credit fears do not touch. The print is the first company data point since the scare.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print came off a sector-driven drawdown of this size. The 2025-11-05 print (+18.0%) came after an AI-bubble scare in tech.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is an inference, not a document, and the 8.3-point put skew says the option market expects the contagion to persist through the print. If the market had separated DOCN from the levered neoclouds, DOCN would not have fallen as much as CoreWeave and IREN over the same 20 days. Sized small.
evidence.independence: Sector credit selloff: https://www.openingbelldailynews.com/p/coreweave-iren-nebius-stock-down-today-oct-22-2026 (2026-10-22). DOCN's own volume on the drop: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-digitalocean-nyse-docn-shares-down-85-whats-next-2026-10-14/ (2026-10-14).

evidence.text: Counterparties that reported after DOCN last spoke show inference and cloud demand still ahead of supply, and GPU pricing rising. Nebius raised on-demand H100/H200/B200/B300 prices 17-21% from 2026-10-01. That is a proxy positive for DOCN's AI ARR and on-demand GPU pricing, which matters for the Q4 guide (exit growth 35%+).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: DOCN's 2026 guide raises (Q1, Q2) came alongside AI ARR growth (+212% in Q2). The Q1 raise drew +40%.
evidence.why_not_priced: These are hyperscaler and peer prints, and DOCN fell alongside them on credit, not demand, grounds. The Q4 guide is where it would show. If priced, DOCN would have bounced with hyperscaler beats. It did not (-4.8% on 2026-10-29). It is a proxy, and only the ~21% AI part of ARR is directly exposed, so it is sized small.
evidence.independence: Proxy. Nebius price increase: https://www.spheron.network/blog/nebius-gpu-price-hike-2026-h100-to-b300-rates-rise-up-to-21/. evidence.text: Capacity-delivery risk, the swing factor UBS named for Q3. UBS (July 2026) said Richmond was near full and that the Kansas City MKC1 ramp was the key Q3 revenue swing. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not observed on a print. The company has said capacity came 'on or ahead of schedule' (2026-08-04 8-K).
evidence.why_not_priced: The incident was a single 8.5-hour event inside a quarter the CFO later reaffirmed (2026-09-11). The Microsoft read-through is a proxy. Small.
evidence.independence: UBS note via search snippet (https://www.itiger.com/news/2573965020). MKC1 incident also on https://isdown.app/status/digitalocean/incidents/640933-degraded-performance-in-mkc1. The CFO statement of 2026-09-11 cuts against this, and the size is net of it.

evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-07-07 RPO pre-release (above $800m) drew +4.3%. RPO has been bought when it jumped. No print yet has shown flat RPO.
evidence.why_not_priced: Previews anchor on another record new ARR and continued RPO growth (Earnings Whispers). If the market expected flat RPO, previews would not set the bar beyond guidance. The sign is unknown: this is a risk with no evidence that Q3 bookings were weak.

evidence.text: On 2026-08-31, with July and August already booked, Herbalife reaffirmed Q3 guidance (net sales +0.5% to +4.5% reported, adj. EBITDA $160-180m, FX assumptions unchanged from Aug 5) and the CFO said the outlook 'remains firmly on track' and the company expects a fifth consecutive quarter of YoY sales growth; this year Q1 sales were pre-released above guide and Q2 sales ($1,326.8m, +5.4%) landed at the top of the range, so a print at or above the $1.31bn Street revenue number is the base case.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Sales beats have not been paid in 2026: Q2 (sales at top of guide) fell -8.65% on an EPS miss; Q1 sales above guide were pre-released 2026-04-14 (+7.34%) and the print itself fell -11.86%. Earlier, 2025-11-05 +11.65% and 2026-02-18 +18.32%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the reaffirmation is public and on the wire. What is less visible is that it was made with two-thirds of the quarter in hand by a CFO who becomes interim CEO on Nov 1, which lowers the probability of a Q3 sales miss; if fully priced, Street revenue would sit at or above the $1.31bn guide upper half rather than at $1.30bn (earningswhispers) and the stock would not trade 10% below its post-Q2 high of $14.89. It lands inside the guided range, so it is sized small.
evidence.independence: Q2 release shows sales at the top of the range (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001180262/000121390026085702/ea030059301ex99-1.htm); same company, different document.

evidence.text: The adj. EPS bar of $0.62-0.63 sits above what the guide midpoint implies: from the Q2 release, adj. EBITDA $166.6m less ~$37m net interest and ~$35m D&A/SaaS amortisation gave ~$94m adj. pretax; at the reaffirmed ~35% FY adj. tax rate and ~104.5m diluted shares, Q3 EBITDA of $160/170/180m maps to roughly $0.53/$0.60/$0.66, so $0.62-0.63 needs ~$173-176m (upper half), and the $0.73 consensus one preview quotes would need EBITDA above the top of the guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: adj. EPS $0.51 vs $0.61-0.63 consensus, driven by a 43.2% adj. tax rate, stock -8.65% despite sales at the top of guide. Q3 2025: adj. EPS $0.50 vs $0.46 consensus, stock +11.65%.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is arithmetic on public numbers that aggregators do not do; the 11% three-month cut in next-quarter EPS estimates (chartmill snippet) shows the Street moved part of the way, but if fully priced the consensus would sit near $0.60, not $0.62-0.73. It is my inference from the guide, not a company EPS guide (there is none), so it is sized small. The bar is disputed ($0.73 in one preview), which caps it.
evidence.independence: Tax rate and interest figures also in the finviz preview (https://finviz.com/news/407924/herbalifes-india-engine-meets-its-gst-anniversary-as-street-bets-on-46-eps-growth, 2026-10-26), which quotes the $0.73/$0.76 numbers; FY ~35% adj. tax rate from the 2026-08-31 release. evidence.text: The FY26 guide was explicitly conditioned on 'category price levels remain stabilized at current levels' (Aug 6 deck, slide 18). That deck's USDA wholesale chart had large white near ~$1.45/dz and rising at week 31. USDA's Egg Markets Overview of Oct 30, 2026 shows national loose large white at $0.35/dz, NY cartoned formula at $0.72/dz and breaking stock at $0.08/dz. VITL sells its excess eggs into the breaker channel, which cost it $19.5M of gross profit in Q2, and a lower conventional price widens its retail price gap. The stated condition for the guide has therefore failed. Revenue consensus ($763.8M) is already below the guide low ($775M), but the Street's FY EPS (-$0.38, implying positive H2 EPS concentrated in Q4) still sits inside the $0-10M EBITDA guide. The exposed number is a cut to the EBITDA or Q4 outlook.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guidance line is what has moved this stock. The Q1 2026 print with a sharp FY cut went -20.67% (2026-05-07). Q4 2025 (2026-02-26), with a weak guide, went -10.81%. Q2 2026, with the guide reaffirmed, went only +2.21% (2026-08-06). Guide raises in 2025 went +17.59% and +16.13%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The revenue half is priced: every Street FY revenue estimate sits below the guide low. The EBITDA half is not visibly priced. If the Street had marked Q4 to $0.35 eggs and $0.08 breaker stock, FY EPS consensus would be at or below H1's -$0.50 rather than at -$0.38, and targets would not average $12.22. Against that, the skew is +4 vol points and the stock is 8% above its low, so some of this sits in the price.
evidence.independence: The company's own guide condition and the Aug wholesale chart are in https://s205.q4cdn.com/845857233/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/v2/Q2-2026-Earnings-Presentation-MASTER-UPDATED.pdf (slides 5 and 18). Trading Economics' egg series shows -23% over the month and -78% over the year as of 2026-11-02 (https://tradingeconomics.com/commodity/eggs-us). This is a proxy for magnitude: the company has not said how much it is exposed. It shares the USDA document with the next finding.

evidence.text: Competitive promotion inside VITL's own tier: USDA's Oct 30 report says 'non-organic free-range and pastured shell eggs continue to be the highest featured among the retail chains'. Pastured brown eggs were featured in 4,236 stores at an average ad price of $5.59/dz and free-range brown in 1,951 stores at $4.61. VITL's own Q2 ARP was $8.16 per EQ unit. The FY guide also assumes 'competitive activity does not intensify further' (Q2 release), and VITL launched its own sub-$5 free-range pilot at Target on Oct 23. Both point to continued pressure on price gaps and price/mix into Q4.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Widening price gaps and competitor promotions were the stated cause of the Q1 2026 miss and cut (-20.67%). The Q2 narrowing of the price gaps came with the guide reaffirmed (+2.21%).
evidence.why_not_priced: USDA feature-activity tables are not on the sell-side wire. If this were priced, previews would be framing the Q4 price/mix risk rather than the Q3 sequential improvement. The analyst target cuts to $8-9 in mid-October may partly reflect it.
evidence.independence: Same USDA document as the finding above, so it counts as a related reading. The company's own free-range pilot under $5 (https://s205.q4cdn.com/845857233/files/doc_news/Vital-Farms-Introduces-a-Higher-Standard-for-Free-Range-Eggs-Through-Limited-Pilot-at-Select-Target-Retail-Stores-2026.pdf, 2026-10-23) independently shows the company moving down the price ladder.

evidence.text: Peer read-through: Cal-Maine's quarter ended Aug 29, 2026 (reported Sep 30) shows specialty shell egg sales -14.0%, with average selling price per dozen -10.7% and volume -3.8%. Specialty segment operating profit fell to $14.9M from $64.2M. Management still called specialty demand 'constructive'. This covers two of the three months of VITL's Q3 and points to continued price/mix deflation in specialty eggs. Q2 VITL revenue was -10.1% YoY; the $182.3M Q3 bar requires sequential growth of about 10% from $166.0M.
